intent: Artifact-only adversarial review of a DECISION or analysis. The reviewer must NOT gather evidence; it reasons solely on an inline ARTIFACT + CONTRACT and emits a machine-readable verdict plus a Claims-To-Verify handoff.

toolAccess.rationale: An artifact-only critic that can read files, run shells/evals, or call MCP tools can (and historically did) gather evidence, misread it, and assert a fabricated fact as a finding. An empty allow-list makes EXTERNAL evidence-gathering, and therefore that specific misattribution failure, STRUCTURALLY impossible rather than merely discouraged by prose. It does NOT prevent inline hallucination (stating a false fact without a tool call); the prompt's Hard Constraints and the claimsToVerify handoff guard that, behaviorally.

denyCategories._note: A VOCABULARY of capability classes a host MAY expose, mapped to concrete tool names by each adapter. Categories that a given host does not have (e.g. 'subagent-spawn' on a host with no subagent API) DO NOT APPLY: an adapter MUST skip them; their absence from a generated artifact is not a conformance violation. Only meaningful at L1 (denylist hosts) and as the L1 hedge beneath L2.

enforcement.note: An adapter MUST emit at the highest level its host supports and MUST warn if the host cannot reach minimumLevel. Below L1, the no-tools contract is advice the model can violate, so the structural guarantee is lost.

L0.name: prompt-only
L0.guarantee: Behavioral only. NO structural enforcement. The 'you have no tools' contract lives only in the prompt; if the host grants tools, the model may still call them. A capable model with a clear prompt often complies, but nothing forces it.
L0.useWhen: The host cannot restrict tools per-agent at all (e.g. a generic chat API where the caller controls tools).

L1.name: denylist
L1.guarantee: Named evidence/mutation tools are removed. Blocks the PRIMARY fabrication path (read-a-log, run-an-eval, write-a-file). KNOWN-INCOMPLETE BY DESIGN: a denylist can only remove tools it can NAME, so anything it cannot enumerate leaks: dynamically-registered MCP/plugin tools (no wildcard on many hosts), newly-added core tools, or skills that internally spawn tool-equipped agents. L1 is a best-effort hedge, never a complete boundary.
L1.useWhen: The host supports a per-agent denylist but not an allow-list, or as a belt-and-suspenders fallback beneath L2.

L2.name: empty-allowlist
L2.guarantee: The agent resolves to ZERO tools, core and MCP. External evidence-gathering is structurally impossible. This is the target level and the ONLY complete boundary, because an allow-list (unlike a denylist) excludes inherited tools it never names, including MCP.
L2.useWhen: The host supports a per-agent allow-list that excludes inherited tools (incl. MCP/plugin tools).

output.note: Hosts that support structured/tool-forced output should validate against output.schema.json so the orchestrator can machine-read claimsToVerify. Hosts without it fall back to the labeled-prose fields named in prompt.md (an adapter for a prose-only host SHOULD assert those field labels are present).
